XXIX ACJM, BENGALURU  JUDGMENT
The P.S.I., of Viveknagara Police Station, Bengaluru, has filed the present charge sheet against the accused for the offence punishable under sections Secs.498A, 506 of IPC.

BRIEF FACTS OF THE PROSECUTION CASE ARE AS UNDER :
It is the case of the complainant that, she got love marriage with accused on 27.08.2019, after marriage, accused picked up quarrel with CW.1 for small small issues and also abused her in filthy language, assaulted her by consuming alcohol and subjected CW.1 to cruelty for dowry by harassing her both physically and mentally and also gave life threat to CW.1.

Based on the typed complaint lodged by C.W.1,
CW.11 has registered the case against accused No.1 to 5 in P.S. Crime No.07/2020 for the offence punishable under sections 498(a) and 506 of IPC.

Investigating Officers/
CW.11 and 12 investigated the matter, after completion of the investigation, CW.12 has submitted final report against the accused No.1 for the offence punishable U/s 498(A), 506 of IPC.
3.
During the crime stage, accused was produced before this court and later on he was released on bail.
Upon receipt of charge sheet, cognizance was taken for the above mentioned offences alleged against the accused and registered the criminal case against him.

After registration of the case, copy of the final report and it's enclosures were furnished to him in compliance of section 207 of Cr.P.C.
Sufficient C.C.No.55447/2020 grounds were made out to frame charges.
Hence, charges framed and read over to the accused.
He pleaded not guilty and claimed to be tried.

4. In order to prove the guilt of the accused, the prosecution has examined one witness out of 12 witnesses cited in the charge sheet as P.W.1 and relied upon documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.04 and closed its side.
Thereafter, the accused was examined as provided U/s 313 of Cr.P.C by explaining incriminating evidence appearing against him.
The accused has denied the same.
5. Heard both sides.
Perused the materials on record.

sentences.text:
The points that arise for my consideration are;
1.

Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, CW.1 got married with accused on 27.08.2019, after the marriage, the accused has abused CW.1, picked up quarrel with her for small issues, assaulted her and also subjected CW.1 to cruelty by harassing her both by physically and mentally for dowry and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.498A of IPC ?
C.C.No.55447/2020 2.
Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubt that, the accused threatened CW.1 with dire consequences and thereby committed an offence punishable U/s.506 of IPC ?
3. What Order?

7. My findings on the above points are as under:
 Point Nos.1 & 2 : In the Negative.
 Point No.3 : As per the final order  for the following;
 REASONS  8. POINT Nos.1 and 2 :-
As these two points are interlinked, I have taken up these points together for common discussion to avoid repetition of facts & evidence.
In order to bring home the guilt of the accused, the pros- ecution has to establish that, accused has picked up quarrel with CW.1, assaulted her, abused her in filthy language and threatened with dire consequences.

. In order prove the above said allegations, the prosecution has examined, the part investigation carried out by the IO i.e., CW.12 as PW.1, wherein, he deposed with regard to the investigation being carried out by him.
He further deposed that, he has recorded the statement of witnesses and after completion of the investigation has filed final report.
PW.1 has further deposed that, as CW.11 has passed away, PW.1 has further deposed with regard to the investigation being carried out by CW.11.
10. On perusal of the entire materials on record, the prosecution has failed to secure the complainant / victim and examine her.
The prosecution has also failed to secure the presence of the mahazar witnesses.
None of the eye witnesses have been examined by the prosecution.

11. On perusal of the materials on record, merely relying on the evidence of CW.12 i.e., the investigating offi- cer, it cannot be concluded that the prosecution has proved its case beyond Ashwini.R vs Vinod Selvam And Others on 1 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117565444/
3 reasonable doubt.

sentences.text: On perusal of the materials on record, the evidence on record is not at all helpful in order to conclude that, the accused has committed the offence as alleged.
Therefore, the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt.
In such circumstances, the benefit of C.C.No.55447/2020 doubt has to be extended to the accused and he is entitled for acquittal.

Accordingly, the Point Nos.1 and 2 are answered in the "Negative".
12.
Point No.3 :-

In view of the findings on above points, I proceed to pass the following;
ORDER
Acting under section 248(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused is acquitted of the offence punishable under Secs.498A and 506 of IPC.
The Bail bond of the accused shall be in force for the period of 6 months and thereafter it shall be cancelled without further orders.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and typed by her, corrected by me and then signed and pronounced in the Open Court on this date the 01 st day of December, 2025.)
